study: Burlando & Bbaale, Fertility Responses to Schooling Costs: Uganda's UPE
policy_or_shock: UPE waived primary fees for up to FOUR children per household; a 5th child's schooling still cost money
design: generalized difference-in-differences: mothers with 4+ primary-age children at onset vs fewer, x policy timing
outcome: probability of an additional birth within 46 months
effect: -4.2 pp probability of another birth within 46 months for mothers whose MARGINAL child would not be fee-exempt; = 8% of the mean
sign_vs_c2b: CONSISTENT — the group facing the higher marginal price of a child had fewer births

study: Keats, Women's schooling, fertility and child health: Uganda's FPE
policy_or_shock: elimination of primary school fees, used as a shock to the WOMAN'S OWN schooling
design: regression discontinuity on the woman's own year of birth / exposure to the reform
effect: +~1 year of schooling at the cutoff; women with more schooling delay and reduce fertility
sign_vs_c2b: NOT APPLICABLE — the estimand is the mother's education, not the price of a child

study: Wakano & Yamada, Terminating universal primary education: Kenya
policy_or_shock: TERMINATION of UPE — a fee REINTRODUCTION, the rare RISE direction
design: fuzzy regression discontinuity; UPE termination instruments female years of education
effect: termination -> -0.57 years female education; 1 extra year of education -> -0.21 children by age 46, onset delayed 0.67 years
sign_vs_c2b: NOT APPLICABLE — estimand is female education, despite the RISE-direction fee shock

study: Winegarden & Murray, Early health-insurance programs, European mortality and fertility
policy_or_shock: government-sponsored health insurance lowering the cost of bearing and rearing children
design: time-series regression on five countries with counterfactual simulation (coverage set to zero)
effect: widening coverage RETARDED the secular decline in marital fertility; the mortality/replacement channel worked the other way
sign_vs_c2b: CONSISTENT — a lower cost of children slowed the fertility decline

study: Ito & Tanaka, Abolishing user fees, fertility choice and educational attainment
setting: South Africa, post-apartheid MCH fee abolition
policy_or_shock: abolition of user fees for maternal and child health services
design: difference-in-differences on exogenous variation in exposure (health-facility availability x timing)
effect: 27-32% reduction in fertility; greater educational attainment of children a decade later
sign_vs_c2b: INCONSISTENT with the simple price mechanism — the price of children FELL and fertility FELL. The authors read it as quantity-quality: cheaper child QUALITY induces substitution toward fewer, better children
routing: ADMIT, sign flagged; jointly informative for C.3.d

study: Xia, Infant Mortality and Desired Fertility: Sierra Leone's Free Health Care Initiative
policy_or_shock: abolition of health user fees for pregnant/breastfeeding women and under-fives
design: difference-in-differences on birth timing x transportation cost to a public facility
effect: no reduction in infant mortality; significant DECLINE in desired fertility, attributed to parents revising infant-mortality expectations (hoarding)
sign_vs_c2b: INCONSISTENT — price fell and desired fertility fell; the stated channel is mortality EXPECTATIONS, which is A.1's replacement/insurance mechanism, not a price effect
routing: BOUNDARY — jointly claimed with A.1, unallocated; DESIRED outcome, never pooled with realized

study: Wanamaker, Fertility and the Price of Children: Slavery and Slave Emancipation
policy_or_shock: changes in slaveholdings alter the marginal product of the slaveowner's OWN children, and hence their net price
design: panel data on slaveowning households, 1850-1870, exploiting exogenous changes in slaveholdings
effect: strong NEGATIVE correlation between own-child prices and fertility
sign_vs_c2b: CONSISTENT — a higher price of children lowers fertility
routing: RE-CELLED from PRICE_SHOCK_FERTILITY. The 'price' here is a SHADOW price net of the child's marginal product as a labour input; scope section 3 assigns the productive VALUE of a child to C.3.a, so this is jointly claimed and unallocated

study: Duflo, Dupas & Kremer, The Impact of Free Secondary Education: Ghana (twins C2B0105, C2B0866)
policy_or_shock: randomised secondary-school scholarships to 2,064 youths; the scholarship pays for the RECIPIENT'S OWN schooling
outcome: ever pregnant by age 22, persisting to 28
effect: female winners 7.0pp less likely to have ever been pregnant by 22, a 14.6% drop on a 47.9% base
sign_vs_c2b: NOT APPLICABLE — the price that fell is the WOMAN'S OWN education, not the price of her children
routing: ROUTE OUT — third fee-abolition study to route out on the maternal-schooling channel

study: Ebenstein, Hazan & Simhon, Changing the Cost of Children and Fertility: the Israeli Kibbutz (twin C2B0849)
policy_or_shock: kibbutzim abandoned equal COST-SHARING of child-rearing, shifting the cost of children onto the parents themselves — a price RISE
design: universal microdata on kibbutz members, exploiting variation in the increase in cost sharing ACROSS kibbutzim
effect: lifetime fertility declined by 0.59 children in the cohorts of affected parents; selective exit by higher-income and lower-fertility couples is examined separately
sign_vs_c2b: CONSISTENT — the cost of children rose and fertility fell
routing: ADMIT. The only SDT-window study in the primary cell, and one of only two clean RISE-direction designs

study: Wanamaker, The United States Fertility Decline: Slavery and Slave Emancipation (MPRA working paper)
routing: TWIN of C2B0128 — the working-paper version of the same study. Counted ONCE
